# CLI reference

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen-reference.sh from `gd --version`: gd 4.0.0. Do not edit by hand. -->

Every `gd` command and option, as printed by `--help`. For a task-by-task guide, start with [Try it in 5 minutes](../getting-started.md); for git equivalents, see [Coming from git](../git-users.md).

## `gd clone`

```text
Create a workspace and check out a ref (lazily, and sparsely with --path)

Usage: gd clone [OPTIONS] <SERVER> <DIR>

Arguments:
  <SERVER>
  <DIR>

Options:
      --ref <REF_NAME>     [default: main]
      --token <TOKEN>      Bearer token for the server ($GD_TOKEN); without one, the token `gd login` saved [env: GD_TOKEN]
      --path <PATHS>       Only materialise these paths (repeatable)
      --objects <OBJECTS>  Fetch objects through a node daemon or regional cache [env: GD_OBJECTS=]
  -h, --help               Print help
  -V, --version            Print version
```

## `gd commit`

```text
Create a changeset on the server from working-copy changes (all, or PATHS)

Usage: gd commit [OPTIONS] --message <MESSAGE> [PATHS]...

Arguments:
  [PATHS]...

Options:
  -m, --message <MESSAGE>
      --token <TOKEN>      Bearer token for the server ($GD_TOKEN); without one, the token `gd login` saved [env: GD_TOKEN]
  -h, --help               Print help
  -V, --version            Print version
```

## `gd land`

```text
Land the committed work on the ref (server-side rebase + atomic ref update). Several commits land one after another, each on the one before

Usage: gd land [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --squash         Land every commit since the last land as one change
      --token <TOKEN>  Bearer token for the server ($GD_TOKEN); without one, the token `gd login` saved [env: GD_TOKEN]
  -h, --help           Print help
  -V, --version        Print version
```

## `gd log`

```text
Changeset history (server-side; no local history needed)

Usage: gd log [OPTIONS] [PATH]

Arguments:
  [PATH]  Limit to a path

Options:
      --rev <REV>
      --token <TOKEN>    Bearer token for the server ($GD_TOKEN); without one, the token `gd login` saved [env: GD_TOKEN]
  -n, --limit <LIMIT>    [default: 20]
      --oneline
      --agent [<AGENT>]  Only what agents landed; with a name, only that agent's (`--agent fix-01`)
      --model <MODEL>    Only changes written with this model (its `Model:` trailer contains MODEL)
  -h, --help             Print help
  -V, --version          Print version
```

## `gd mount`

```text
Mount a revision read-only; files are fetched on first read (Linux, macOS, Windows)

Usage: gd mount [OPTIONS] <DIR>

Arguments:
  <DIR>

Options:
      --server <SERVER>
      --token <TOKEN>        Bearer token for the server ($GD_TOKEN); without one, the token `gd login` saved [env: GD_TOKEN]
      --objects <OBJECTS>    Daemon or cache serving objects
      --rev <REV>            [default: main]
      --cache-mb <CACHE_MB>  In-memory cache for file contents [default: 256]
      --serve-only           Serve the checkout over NFS on localhost and print the command that mounts it, instead of mounting (for machines where only an administrator may mount, or Linux machines without FUSE)
  -h, --help                 Print help
  -V, --version              Print version
```

## `gd mcp`

```text
Serve Grovedock as MCP tools over stdio for AI agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor...)

Usage: gd mcp [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --server <SERVER>

      --token <TOKEN>
          Bearer token for the server ($GD_TOKEN); without one, the token `gd login` saved [env: GD_TOKEN]
      --http <ADDR>
          Serve the whole server to remote agents over HTTP at this address (e.g. 0.0.0.0:7430), instead of one workspace over stdio. Each request's bearer token is passed through to the server
      --allowed-host <ALLOWED_HOSTS>
          Host names clients use to reach the HTTP endpoint (repeatable); default: loopback only, against DNS rebinding
      --allowed-origin <ALLOWED_ORIGINS>
          Browser origins allowed to call the HTTP endpoint (repeatable), e.g. https://app.example.com:443; default: none (requests with an Origin are refused)
  -h, --help
          Print help
  -V, --version
          Print version
```

## `gd repo`

```text
Create and list repositories on a server that hosts many (`grovedockd server --platform`)

Usage: gd repo [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  create  Create OWNER/NAME. Then: `gd clone SERVER/OWNER/NAME`
  list    List repositories, optionally of one owner
  grant   Give a person, agent or team (ORG/TEAM) a role on a repository; `none` removes it. With only the repository, lists who has access
  help    Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --token <TOKEN>  Bearer token for the server ($GD_TOKEN); without one, the token `gd login` saved [env: GD_TOKEN]
  -h, --help           Print help
  -V, --version        Print version
```

```text
      --token <TOKEN>              Bearer token for the server ($GD_TOKEN); without one, the token `gd login` saved [env: GD_TOKEN]
      --server <SERVER>
  -h, --help                       Print help
  -V, --version                    Print version
```

```text

```

## `gd cr`

```text
Change requests: propose a branch, review it, land it

Usage: gd cr [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  create      Propose a branch for landing on another: `gd cr create --title "…"`
  list        List change requests
  view        Show one, with what still blocks it
  comment     Comment, on the change or on a line of a file
  review      Approve, request changes, or comment
  check       Report a CI check on the current version: `gd cr check 12 build passed --url …`
  land        Land it, once nothing blocks it
  rebase      Replay it on the target's tip; files both changed merge line by line
  conflicts   Where it clashes with its target: each file's merge, with conflict markers. `--write DIR` saves them as DIR/PATH to edit, for `gd cr resolve --from DIR`
  undo-agent  Undo everything an agent landed on a branch since a time, as one change request. Later edits by people stay where they don't overlap; files where they do are left and listed
  resolve     Settle its clashes: each clashing file is read from DIR/PATH (markers removed), then the branch is replayed on the target's tip
  ready       Mark a draft ready for review
  close
  reopen
  help        Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --server <SERVER>  The repository, SERVER/OWNER/NAME; defaults to the workspace's
      --token <TOKEN>    Bearer token for the server ($GD_TOKEN); without one, the token `gd login` saved [env: GD_TOKEN]
  -h, --help             Print help
  -V, --version          Print version
```

### `gd cr create`

```text
Propose a branch for landing on another: `gd cr create --title "…"`

Usage: gd cr create [OPTIONS] --title <TITLE>

Options:
      --server <SERVER>        The repository, SERVER/OWNER/NAME; defaults to the workspace's
      --title <TITLE>
      --token <TOKEN>          Bearer token for the server ($GD_TOKEN); without one, the token `gd login` saved [env: GD_TOKEN]
      --body <BODY>            [default: ""]
      --source <SOURCE>        The branch to land; defaults to the workspace's branch
      --target <TARGET>        Where to land it; defaults to the repository's default branch [default: ""]
      --draft
      --reviewer <REVIEWERS>   Ask someone to review (repeatable)
      --upstream <OWNER/NAME>  Propose it to the repository this one was forked from (OWNER/NAME); reading that repository is enough
  -h, --help                   Print help
  -V, --version                Print version
```

```text

      --author <AUTHOR>  Only this author; `agent/*` for every agent [default: ""]
  -q, --query <QUERY>    Search, e.g. `is:ready reviewer:@me into:main tax` [default: ""]
      --limit <LIMIT>    How many to show (at most 200); the total is printed after [default: 50]
  -h, --help             Print help
  -V, --version          Print version
```

### `gd cr check`

```text
Report a CI check on the current version: `gd cr check 12 build passed --url …`

Usage: gd cr check [OPTIONS] <NUMBER> <NAME> <STATE>

Arguments:
  <NUMBER>
  <NAME>
  <STATE>   [possible values: pending, passed, failed, skipped]

      --server <SERVER>    The repository, SERVER/OWNER/NAME; defaults to the workspace's
```

## `gd release`

```text
Releases: a tag with notes written from what landed, and files

Usage: gd release [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  list
  view      A release (`latest` for the newest that isn't a pre-release)
  notes     Notes for a release from what landed since the previous one, and the version that fits
  create    Release a tag, making it at `--at` if it doesn't exist. Notes are written from what landed unless `--notes` or `--notes-file` gives them
  publish   Publish a draft: it's dated now and announced
  edit
  upload    Attach files (a file of the same name is replaced)
  download  Download a release's files into a folder (default: here)
  link      A link that downloads one file for ten minutes without signing in (for curl, CI, a browser)
  detach    Remove a file from a release
  delete    Delete a release; its tag stays. Published releases: administrators only
  help      Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --server <SERVER>  The repository, SERVER/OWNER/NAME; defaults to the workspace's
      --token <TOKEN>    Bearer token for the server ($GD_TOKEN); without one, the token `gd login` saved [env: GD_TOKEN]

  -V, --version          Print version
```

```text
Take jobs and run them until stopped
```

### `gd token create`

```text
Create a token. Prints it once: store it as GD_TOKEN

Usage: gd token create [OPTIONS] <NAME>

Arguments:
  <NAME>


Options:
      --as <ACTS_AS>
          Act as an agent you answer for, e.g. `agent/refactor-07` (created if new)

      --server <SERVER>


      --token <TOKEN>
          Bearer token for the server ($GD_TOKEN); without one, the token `gd login` saved

          [env: GD_TOKEN]

      --repo <REPOSITORIES>
          Only these repositories, OWNER/NAME or OWNER/* for all of an organisation's (repeatable); default: all you can reach

      --role <ROLE>
          Highest role the token may use

          Possible values:
          - read
          - triage
          - write
          - maintain
          - admin
          - none:     Removes the member or grant

          [default: write]

      --days <DAYS>
          Days until it expires (1–366)

          [default: 90]

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

  -V, --version
          Print version
```

## `gd migrate`

```text
Move a repository from any git host to Grovedock: full history, and from GitHub, open pull requests (as change requests) and issues with their comments

Usage: gd migrate [OPTIONS] --to <TO> <FROM>

Arguments:
  <FROM>  Where it is now: any URL git can clone

Options:
      --to <TO>
          Where it goes: SERVER/OWNER/NAME
      --token <TOKEN>
          Bearer token for the server ($GD_TOKEN); without one, the token `gd login` saved [env: GD_TOKEN]
      --github-token <GITHUB_TOKEN>
          For private GitHub repositories, and to avoid GitHub's rate limit. Prefer the GD_GITHUB_TOKEN (or GITHUB_TOKEN) environment variable or --github-token-file: a value given here is visible to other users of the machine (`ps`) [env: GD_GITHUB_TOKEN]
      --github-token-file <GITHUB_TOKEN_FILE>
          Read the GitHub token from this file
      --no-issues
          Skip issues
      --no-pull-requests
          Skip pull requests
      --github-api <GITHUB_API>
          GitHub Enterprise Server's API, e.g. https://github.example.com/api/v3
  -h, --help
          Print help
  -V, --version
          Print version
```

## `gd mirror`

```text
Keep a git repository (GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, any git remote) up to date with a branch: every landed change becomes the same git commit every time, pushed without force

Usage: gd mirror [OPTIONS] --to <TO>

Options:
      --to <TO>            Where to push: any URL git accepts. Credentials come from git (SSH keys or a credential helper)
      --token <TOKEN>      Bearer token for the server ($GD_TOKEN); without one, the token `gd login` saved [env: GD_TOKEN]
      --server <SERVER>
      --rev <REV>          [default: main]
      --git-ref <GIT_REF>  [default: main]
      --dir <DIR>          The mirror's local copy (a bare git repository); defaults to the user cache
      --every <SECONDS>    Mirror again every SECONDS until interrupted; without it, mirror once and exit
  -h, --help               Print help
  -V, --version            Print version
```
